# Surge Geosite

> Surge Geosite converts `v2fly/domain-list-community` geosite datasets into ready-to-use Surge rulesets. It also exposes cached/mirrored sing-box `.srs` and Mihomo `.mrs` artifacts for the same list names where available.

`balanced` is the normal default mode. `strict` and `full` exist for explicit conversion tradeoffs.

## Project Overview

Surge Geosite is an HTTP service and dashboard for discovering geosite lists and generating rule URLs. It is designed for specific rule URL generation, not for mirroring the entire dataset.

The main human entry points are:

- [English dashboard](https://surge.bojin.co/en)
- [Chinese dashboard](https://surge.bojin.co/zh)

The main machine entry point is:

- [`/geosite`](https://surge.bojin.co/geosite)

## Common Task Flow

For simple usage discovery, `/geosite` provides the available list index. `balanced` is the normal mode for Surge rulesets. `strict` is the conservative mode, and `full` is the broadest mode with more over-match risk.

Filters use the `{name}@{filter}` suffix, such as `apple@cn`. sing-box artifacts are under `/geosite-srs/{name}`. Mihomo artifacts are under `/geosite-mrs/{name}`.

Artifacts are intended for specific on-demand URLs. Bulk fetching every list, mode, and filter combination is discouraged.

## API Reference

### `GET /geosite`

Returns the available geosite index. This endpoint provides list names and known filters.

Index contents:

- List names such as `google`, `apple`, or `category-ads-all`.
- Sorted filter arrays for each list.
- An empty array means no known filters for that list.

Approximate JSON shape:

```json
{
  "apple": ["cn"],
  "google": []
}
```

### `GET /geosite/{name}`

Returns a Surge ruleset using default `balanced` mode.

`/geosite/google` is equivalent to `/geosite/balanced/google`.

Example:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite/google
```

### `GET /geosite/{mode}/{name}`

Returns a Surge ruleset using the selected mode. The response body is `text/plain`; each non-empty line is a Surge rule such as `DOMAIN-SUFFIX,example.com`.

Valid modes:

- `strict`
- `balanced`
- `full`

Example:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite/balanced/google
```

### `GET /geosite/{mode}/{name}@{filter}`

Returns a `text/plain` Surge ruleset containing only entries tagged with the selected filter.

Example:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite/balanced/apple@cn
```

If a client requires URL encoding, encode `@` as `%40`:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite/balanced/apple%40cn
```

### `GET /geosite-srs/{name}`

Returns a cached/mirrored sing-box `.srs` artifact for a list name.

Example:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite-srs/google
```

### `GET /geosite-mrs/{name}`

Returns a cached/mirrored Mihomo `.mrs` artifact for a list name.

Example:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite-mrs/google
```

## Regex Modes

### `balanced`

Normal default. It provides a controlled conversion strategy suitable for normal use.

### `strict`

Most conservative conversion. Unsupported or non-lossless regex conversion is skipped.

### `full`

Most permissive conversion. It aims for maximum coverage and can have higher over-match risk. It is not the normal default mode.

## Names And Filters

- List names are lowercase.
- Examples: `google`, `apple`, `github`, `category-ads-all`.
- Filters are lowercase attributes appended with `@`.
- Example: `apple@cn` means list `apple` filtered to entries tagged `cn`.
- Not all lists have filters. `/geosite` contains sorted known filter arrays.

## URL Encoding

Path examples in documentation may show raw `@` for readability:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite/balanced/apple@cn
```

When constructing URLs programmatically, encode the combined `{name}@{filter}` path segment if needed:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite/balanced/apple%40cn
```

Slashes are not valid inside list names. List names and filters are validated and invalid values return `400`.

## ETag And Conditional Requests

Responses are cache-friendly and include `ETag` headers where applicable.

Supported HTTP behavior:

- `ETag` can identify a response version.
- `If-None-Match` is supported for conditional requests where applicable.
- `304 Not Modified` means the representation has not changed.
- The upstream geosite source changes on its own schedule.

Some responses can include stale fallback behavior while fresh artifacts are rebuilt in the background. If the `x-stale: 1` header is present, the body is a previous artifact served intentionally to keep the service responsive.

## Errors

- `400 invalid name`: The list name, filter, mode, or path encoding is invalid.
- `404 list not found`: The requested geosite list does not exist.
- `404 srs not found`: The requested sing-box SRS artifact was not found upstream.
- `404 mrs not found`: The requested Mihomo MRS artifact was not found upstream.
- `503 geosite data not ready`: The service has not finished preparing initial geosite data.

`503` indicates temporary unavailability while data is not ready.

## Cookbooks

### Give a user a Surge URL for Google

Example balanced-mode URL:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite/balanced/google
```

### Give a user a Surge URL for Apple CN entries

Example balanced-mode URL with a filter:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite/balanced/apple@cn
```

### Give a user a sing-box SRS URL

Example SRS endpoint:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite-srs/google
```

### Give a user a Mihomo MRS URL

Example MRS endpoint:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite-mrs/google
```

### Discover available lists

Index endpoint:

```text
https://surge.bojin.co/geosite
```

The response is the source of truth for available list names.

## Data Source And Refresh

The source of truth is [`v2fly/domain-list-community`](https://github.com/v2fly/domain-list-community). The service periodically checks upstream changes and refreshes snapshots when upstream changes are detected.

Generated artifacts are cached by upstream version, mode, list name, and optional filter. Some artifacts are built on demand and reused after the first request.

## Operational Notes And Limits

- Bulk fetching every `/geosite/{mode}/{name}` combination is discouraged.
- Bulk fetching every filter combination is discouraged.
- `full` is not the safest or default mode.
- Not every list has filters.
- SRS and MRS artifacts may not exist for every geosite list.
- `503` responses indicate temporary data readiness issues.
- This file is documentation, not a full dump of upstream geosite data.
